source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #354 (branch fix/319-decoder-strictness at head c965df7ea3720c33fab6283cb02de5eb947e1e24 — the #319 change (the component decoder parses every section body through a size-limited reader and must consume it exactly, custom sections validate their name, and core/component decode errors keep the spec reasons: `unexpected end-of-file`, `integer too large`, `malformed UTF-8 encoding`) merged with current main b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b (PR #353), with no merge conflicts; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45610872278, 45610879531 and 45610885686 against the branch and pull-request run 45610864030, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #354 (#319, component section sizes are enforced and core decode reasons are preserved). The branch merged current main (merge commit 1eba0c7, main at b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b — PR #353 (#318) on top of the 21edef0 main the branch was based on); the merge was conflict-free, and its CI run on the merged tree tripped the gate. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45610897012, 45610904920 and 45610913665 on main at b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b): the main control is byte-identical to the checked-in baseline on all 32 gated series. This PR's own delta against the main control splits by configuration family. The four core configurations grow slightly in both profiles — release stripped file +304 B (core), +320 B (core-nosimd), +272 B (core-jit), +256 B (core-aot) and stripped .text +176/+176/+144/+144 B; release-size stripped file +512/+512/+416/+432 B and stripped .text +304/+320/+240/+240 B — the new WasmParserError::IntegerTooLarge variant and the format_io_error helper in the telomere library. The three configurations that link telomere-component shrink substantially — release stripped file −123,960 B (component), −123,976 B (wasi), −123,992 B (wasi-threads) and stripped .text −112,064 B in each; release-size stripped file −69,208/−69,192/−69,144 B and stripped .text −63,248/−63,248/−63,216 B — because every section body is now parsed through the take() size-limited reader, so the generic section parsers are monomorphized for a single reader type instead of two (previously only the CoreModule and Component sections used a limited reader). The baseline configuration is unchanged. Following the established practice of re-baselining growth only (the gate passes shrinkage), the sixteen exceeding core series are re-baselined to the branch measurements and the twelve shrunken component series keep their PR #353 baselines, so those baselines now sit above the measured sizes by the amounts above until a future re-baseline absorbs the shrinkage. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the four branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release component stripped file series at +11.02% (2,433,656 B to 2,701,856 B, the retained PR #353 baseline; the branch itself measures 2,577,896 B, +5.93%); the release core-nosimd stripped file series rises from +9.83% to +9.86% (1,275,448 B to 1,401,160 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
